XII, 10; Corinth 6, p. 152, no. 4; Agora 2, p. 76, no. 1935; Corinth 3.1, p. 66-67, argues that the series with “Corinti” was issued by Guilaume de Villerhardouin and that with “Corintum” by Geoffrey II de Villehardouin (1218-1245).  The line of evidence he adduced, the relative number of the types preserved, is now clearer.  Thus, Corinth 6 reported 137 for “Corinti” and Castle Gate, 194 for “Corintum” and Acrocorinth; and Agora 2, reported 49 for the former and 276 for the latter.  The total for these two sites are “Cortini” 186 and “Corintum” 470, strengthening the conclusion that the latter were struck by Geoffrey (1218-45) and the former by William (1245-50), before the establishment of the mint at Clarenza.  The “Genoese” gate thus becomes  a gate of Acrocorinth, as Bellinger argued in Corinth 3.2.
